title: Share or Group? Prove It!
goal: I can tell if a story is sharing or grouping, find the missing number, and confirm my answer by multiplying.

card.desc: Prove-it day for division. In class Bailey decides whether a story is sharing (how many in each) or grouping (how many groups), finds unknowns anywhere in a fact family, and confirms every answer by multiplying. The after-class lesson and break work are spread week by week until Lesson 12. Seven new words, including divisible and daunting.

win: You proved it: division undoes multiplication, and you can check every answer!

slides.title: On Your Own: Share or Group? Prove It!
slides.text: In class you sorted sharing and grouping stories and confirmed answers by multiplying. Now you prove it on your own. It takes about 25 minutes and ends with Show What You Know.

slides.title: Teach it to someone
slides.text: Find someone at home. Teach them. Say it out loud before you go on.
prompts: Tell them the difference between a sharing story and a grouping story. Make up a dragon example of each.
Show them how to confirm 43 ÷ 8 = 5 R 3 by multiplying.
What is one thing in How to Train Your Dragon that Hiccup had to decipher or interpret?
starters: A sharing story … A grouping story …
To confirm it, I multiply … then add …

slides.title: Remember the words
slides.text: Tap each card. Say the meaning before you flip it. Then flip to check yourself.

words.meaning: To show for sure that something is true or right.
The missing number you need to find in a problem.
Able to be divided by a number with nothing left over.
To figure out what something means.
words.example: Interpret the story: is it sharing, or making groups?

words.meaning: To figure out something that is hard to read or understand, like a code.
words.example: Hiccup could decipher Dragonese, the language of dragons.

words.meaning: Exactly right, with every detail correct.
Seeming hard or scary to do, before you start.
words.example: Big division problems look daunting, but one fact at a time makes them easy.

slides.title: Interpret, solve, confirm
slides.text: Sharing: you know the number of groups, find how many in each. Grouping: you know how many in each, find the number of groups.
slides.tip: Never trust an answer until you confirm it.

slides.title: Sharing or grouping?
slides.text: Tap a story. Then tap the box that tells what the story asks.

items.text: Fishlegs puts 48 eggs into nests of 8. How many nests?
items.why: You know how many in each nest (8). You find how many nests.
items.hint: Is 8 the number of nests, or the eggs in each nest?

items.text: 56 Vikings sit at 7 tables, the same number at each. How many at each table?
items.why: You know the groups (7 tables). You find how many at each.
items.hint: Do you know how many tables there are?

items.text: Hiccup reads 9 pages a night. How many nights to read 72 pages?
items.why: Each night is a group of 9 pages. You find how many nights.
items.hint: 9 pages go in each night. What are you finding?

items.text: Stoick shares 36 apples equally among 6 children. How many apples does each child get?
items.why: You know the groups (6 children). You find how many each gets.
items.hint: Do you know how many children there are?

items.text: Toothless carries 6 fish per trip. How many trips to move 54 fish?
items.why: Each trip is a group of 6 fish. You find how many trips.
items.hint: 6 fish go in each trip. What are you finding?

items.text: 63 shields are hung evenly on 9 walls. How many on each wall?
items.why: You know the groups (9 walls). You find how many on each.
items.hint: Do you know how many walls there are?

slides.done: Same division, different question. Interpret the story before you solve it.

slides.title: Confirm it
slides.text: Type the number you get when you check.

items.why: 7 × 9 = 63. It matches the dividend, so 63 ÷ 9 = 7 is confirmed.
7 × 6 = 42 and 42 + 3 = 45. It matches, so the answer is confirmed.

items.q: Snotlout wrote 48 ÷ 6 = 7. Check: 7 × 6 = 42, not 48. What is the right quotient?
Fishlegs wrote 60 ÷ 8 = 7 R 4. Check it. What do you find?
items.why: 7 × 8 = 56 and 56 + 4 = 60. It is confirmed.
no: 12 left over is more than 8. One more group fits.

items.q: ? ÷ 8 = 7. What is the unknown?
54 ÷ ? = 9. What is the unknown?
A fact family has 6 and 42. The biggest number is 42. What is the third number?
items.why: 6 × 7 = 42, so the family is 6, 7 and 42.

slides.title: Story problems
slides.text: Interpret, solve, confirm. Type the number.

items.q: Stoick has 64 fish. He gives 8 to each dragon. How many dragons does he feed?
items.why: Grouping: 64 ÷ 8 = 8 dragons. Confirm: 8 × 8 = 64.
items.no: Is 8 the dragons, or the fish for each dragon?

items.q: 49 Vikings row in 7 boats, the same number in each boat. How many Vikings in each boat?
items.why: Sharing: 49 ÷ 7 = 7 in each boat. Confirm: 7 × 7 = 49.

items.q: Hiccup has 58 arrows. He puts 8 in each quiver. How many quivers can he fill, and how many arrows are left?
no: 8 × 8 = 64. That is more arrows than he has.
10 left is more than 8. Another quiver can be filled.

items.q: To figure out what a story means and what it asks is to ____ it. (Use a word from your word cards.)
items.why: To interpret is to figure out what something means.

items.q: 56 can be divided by 8 with nothing left over. 56 is ____ by 8. (Use a word from your word cards.)
items.why: Divisible means able to be divided with nothing left over.
items.no: It starts with d and ends with -ible.

items.q: The mountain looked daunting, but Hiccup began the climb. Which word means almost the same as daunting?
items.why: Daunting means it seems hard or scary before you begin.
no: Daunting describes how it feels before you start.

items.q: 38 ÷ 9 = ____   (use R for the remainder)
Use the area model: 47 × 6 = ____

sets.q: ? ÷ 9 = 4. What is the unknown?
72 ÷ ? = 8. What is the unknown?
Only one division is correct. Check each one. Which is it?
Stoick shares 48 fish equally among 6 dragons. What kind of story is it? Type sharing or grouping.
sets.why: You know the groups (6 dragons). You find how many fish each gets: 48 ÷ 6 = 8.
sets.no: Is 6 the number of dragons, or the fish for each dragon?

sets.q: Hiccup puts 63 arrows into quivers. Each quiver holds 9. How many quivers does he fill?
Snotlout wrote 38 ÷ 7 = 5 R 3. Check it. What do you find?
Three facts from one family: 8 × 7 = 56, 56 ÷ 7 = 8, 56 ÷ 8 = 7. Which multiplication fact is missing? Type it.
sets.why: The missing fact is the turn-around: 7 × 8 = 56.

sets.q: Which number is divisible by 7?
To show for sure that an answer is right is to ____ it. (Use a word from your word cards.)
sets.why: To confirm is to show for sure that something is true or right.

sets.q: To confirm that 42 ÷ 6 = 7, you should…
choices: multiply 7 × 6 and see if you get 42
add 42 + 6 and see if you get 48
ask a friend for the answer
no: Adding does not check a division.
That is backward and does not check anything.
Confirming means checking it yourself with math.

sets.q: ? ÷ 9 = 7. What is the unknown?
48 ÷ ? = 6. What is the unknown?
Check each division. Only one is correct. Which one?
Fishlegs ties 56 arrows into bundles of 8. What kind of story is it? Type sharing or grouping.
sets.why: You know how many go in each bundle (8). You find how many bundles: 56 ÷ 8 = 7.
sets.no: Is 8 the number of bundles, or the arrows in each bundle?

sets.q: Stoick shares 81 fish equally among 9 dragons. How many fish does each dragon get?
Hiccup wrote 50 ÷ 6 = 8 R 2. Check it. What do you find?
no: 8 left over is more than 6. One more group fits.

sets.q: Two facts in a family are 9 × 6 = 54 and 54 ÷ 9 = 6. Finish this one: 54 ÷ 6 = ____
sets.no: Which number has not been the answer yet?

sets.q: Which number is divisible by 8?
The missing number you need to find in a problem is the ____. (Use a word from your word cards.)
sets.why: The unknown is the missing number you need to find.
sets.no: It means not known yet. It starts with u.

sets.q: The test looked daunting. How did it seem before Bailey started?
sets.why: Daunting means it seems hard or scary before you begin.
no: Daunting describes how it feels before you start.

sets.q: ? ÷ 6 = 8. What is the unknown?
40 ÷ ? = 5. What is the unknown?
Snotlout checked four answers. Which one is confirmed?
63 fish are split evenly among 7 dragons. What kind of story is it? Type sharing or grouping.
sets.why: You know the groups (7 dragons). You find how many each gets: 63 ÷ 7 = 9.
sets.no: Is 7 the number of dragons, or the fish for each dragon?

sets.q: Toothless eats 6 fish a day. How many days will 54 fish last?
sets.no: Each day is a group of 6. Ask: 6 × what = 54?

sets.q: Fishlegs wrote 61 ÷ 8 = 7 R 6. Check it. What do you find?
choices: Wrong: 7 × 8 + 6 = 62, so it should be 7 R 5
no: 13 left over is more than 8. One more group fits.

sets.q: A fact family has 8 and 72. The biggest number is 72. What is the third number?
Which number is divisible by 9?
To figure out a code or something hard to read is to ____ it. (Use a word from your word cards.)
sets.why: To decipher is to figure out something hard to read or understand, like a code.
sets.no: Hiccup did it with Dragonese. It starts with d.

sets.q: Be precise. What is 52 ÷ 7?
sets.why: 7 × 7 = 49 and 52 − 49 = 3. Precise means the exact answer: 7 R 3.
no: "About" is not precise. Give the exact answer.
You left out the 3 left over.

practice.intro: Three tries on each one, but only your first try counts. Interpret the story, solve it, and confirm it by multiplying.

questions.q: Toothless eats 9 crabs a day. How many days will 63 crabs last?
Fishlegs has 36 dragon cards. He makes piles of 6. What does the story not tell you yet?
choices: How many cards in each pile?
no: The story already tells you: 6 in each pile.
The story already tells you: 36 cards in all.

questions.q: 42 Vikings form 7 equal rows. How many Vikings are in each row?
Only one is correct. Check each one. Which is it?
Check 46 ÷ 9 = 5 R 1. What do you find?
no: A remainder must be smaller than the divisor.

questions.why: 8 × 6 = 48 and 48 + 5 = 53. It matches, so it is confirmed.

questions.q: To figure out what a word problem means and what it asks is to ____ it. (Use a word from your word cards.)
questions.why: To interpret is to figure out what something means.

questions.q: Exactly right, with every detail correct, is ____. (Use a word from your word cards.)
questions.why: Precise means exactly right, with every detail correct.

questions.q: The climb up the cliff looked daunting. Which word means almost the same?
questions.why: Daunting means it looks hard or scary before you start.
no: Divisible is a math word about dividing.

teacher.objective: Bailey proves the week: she interprets division stories as sharing (find how many in each) or grouping (find how many groups), finds unknowns in any spot of a fact family (? ÷ 8 = 9, 63 ÷ ? = 9), solves mixed 6–9 division facts, and confirms every answer by multiplying (quotient × divisor + remainder = dividend).
materials: Class lesson on your laptop or tablet (teacher code 9110)
Her fact family index cards from Lessons 9 and 10
6 sticky notes labeled Sharing or Grouping (3 of each)
Her book, How to Train Your Dragon
Packet (2 pages): done during the break

plan.do: Class slide 1. Beans, 8 cups, whiteboard, her fact family cards, 6 Sharing/Grouping sticky notes. Ask about Tuesday's check and the Lesson 9 packet.
Class slide 2. Hiccup's biggest problem, how he solves problems with his brain, and one week word that fits a real moment.
Class slide 3. She explains each answer, including why the remainder is smaller than the divisor.
Class slide 4. She uses each word to describe something from this week; divisible linked to no remainder; daunting plus what she did about it.
Class slides 5–6. 42 beans shared onto 7 plates vs piles of 7 with sticky-note labels; four stories decided out loud, two acted out with beans.
Class slides 7–8. Whiteboard rule: quotient × divisor (+ remainder) = dividend. She writes each check before answering.
Class slides 9–10. Which part is missing (dividend, divisor, quotient)? Cover the corner on a fact family card; multiply when the dividend is missing.
Class slides 11–12. Six steps from memory onto the whiteboard, then each story solved out loud: interpret, divide, confirm, label.
Class slide 13. Clue words; daunting in a sentence about the break.

Class slides 14–15. Three items on her own (note any miss for Lesson 12); then the break plan on the course page: first week After-class lesson, Lesson 11 Practice and Lesson 10 Packet page 2; second week Lesson 11 Packet and Division Station 4; third week Division Station 5; reading every week.

watch: Adding or subtracting the two numbers in a story (63 − 9 = 54) instead of dividing. Ask: is the total being split up? Then it is division.
Mixing up the label: answering "8 groups of dragons" when the story asks how many fish each dragon gets. Ask: what does your answer count?
For ? ÷ 8 = 9, adding 8 + 9 = 17. Ask: which number is missing, and which is the biggest number in this family? 9 × 8 = 72.
Confirming with the wrong operation, or forgetting to add the remainder when checking (6 × 7 + 2). Point to the whiteboard rule.
Picking a long method (drawing 72 dots) when a fact works. Praise the drawing once, then ask: which fact gives this faster?
"I can't do it" on a word problem. Say: "It looks daunting. What is the first detective step?" and wait.

packet_key.answer: confirm → to show for sure that something is true; unknown → the missing number in a problem; divisible → can be divided with nothing left over; interpret → to figure out what something means; decipher → to figure out something hard to read, like a code; precise → exactly right in every detail; daunting → seeming hard or scary before you start
Grouping; 52 ÷ 7 = 7 R 3: 7 full piles, 3 pebbles left; 7 × 7 + 3 = 52
Answers vary. Example: The divisor is 9. 9 × 8 = 72, so the quotient is 8. I confirm it by multiplying 8 × 9 = 72.
Answers vary; a real moment from the book, daunting used correctly, and what Hiccup did.

slides.title: Share or Group? Prove It!
slides.text: This week you learned that division undoes multiplication, met fact families, and found leftovers. Today you prove it: figure out what a story is asking, find missing numbers, and check every answer by multiplying.

notes.do: Set out: about 65 beans (63 are needed for the Toothless story), 8 cups, whiteboard, her fact family cards from Lessons 9 and 10, and 6 sticky notes (3 say Sharing, 3 say Grouping).
notes.say: "Prove-it day. No new big idea, just one new habit: you never trust an answer until you check it."
notes.ask: "How did Tuesday's Show What You Know go? Did the Lesson 9 packet feel easy or hard?" (Check her scores and the packet before class.)

slides.title: The big problem
slides.text: Think about How to Train Your Dragon.
prompts: What is the biggest problem in the part you read? Who or what is Hiccup up against?
Hiccup is not the biggest or strongest Viking. What does he use instead to solve problems? Give an example.
Pick a word from this week (ration, provisions, scarce, surplus, hesitate, negotiate) that fits a moment in the story. Explain why it fits.

notes.do: 7 minutes. This is the last book talk before the break, so ask her where she will be in the book by Lesson 12.
notes.ask: "Hiccup is not the strongest Viking. What does he use instead? Give one example." Then the word prompt: she picks a week word that fits a real moment.
notes.listen: She names a skill (thinking, studying dragons, talking to Toothless) and backs it with an event. For the word prompt, the moment must actually fit the meaning.

items.q: 34 ÷ 8 = ____   (use R for the remainder)
Which word means an extra amount, more than needed?
items.why: A surplus is extra.
no: Scarce means very little, the opposite.
The quotient is the answer to a division.
Hesitate means to stop for a moment.

items.q: 72 ÷ 9 = 8 is in a fact family. Which fact is in the same family?
items.why: The family is 8, 9 and 72: 72 ÷ 8 = 9.
no: Backward. The biggest number comes first.
Subtraction is not in this family.

notes.ask: "Why is 2 the remainder and not 10?" (10 is bigger than 8; another group fits.)
notes.listen: She explains every answer out loud. Quick and confident here means Tuesday stuck.

slides.title: Words for today
slides.text: Tap each card to flip it. Read it out loud. Then use it to describe something you did this week.

words.meaning: To show for sure that something is true or right.
The missing number you need to find in a problem.
Able to be divided by a number with nothing left over.
To figure out what something means.
words.example: Interpret the story: is it sharing, or making groups?

words.meaning: To figure out something that is hard to read or understand, like a code.
words.example: Hiccup could decipher Dragonese, the language of dragons.

words.meaning: Exactly right, with every detail correct.
Seeming hard or scary to do, before you start.
words.example: Big division problems look daunting, but one fact at a time makes them easy.

notes.do: She reads each card and uses it to describe something from this week. Write confirm and unknown on the whiteboard.
notes.say: "Three of these words are about being a detective: interpret, decipher, confirm. That is what you are today."
notes.ask: "Which number is divisible by 8: 48 or 50? How do you know?" "Tell me something that felt daunting this week, and what you did about it."
notes.listen: Divisible = nothing left over (connect to Tuesday's remainders). For daunting, steer her to say what she DID, not just that it was hard.

slides.title: Two kinds of division stories
slides.text: A division story gives you the total and one more number. Interpret the story: what does the other number tell you?

steps.text: Sharing: 42 dragon eggs are shared equally among 7 nests. You know the number of groups (7 nests). Find how many in each.
Grouping: 42 dragon eggs, 7 in each nest. You know how many go in each (7). Find how many groups.
Both are 42 ÷ 7 = 6. Only the label changes: 6 eggs in each nest, or 6 nests.

slides.tip: Sharing story? The answer is how many in each. Grouping story? The answer is how many groups.

notes.do: Hands-on: 42 beans shared onto 7 plates (she puts a Sharing sticky note on it). Then 42 beans in piles of 7 (Grouping sticky note). Leave both setups on the table.
notes.say: "Monday you called these 'how many in each' and 'how many groups'. Today they get short names: sharing and grouping."
notes.ask: "In both setups, what did the 7 tell you?" (Sharing: 7 groups. Grouping: 7 in each.)
notes.listen: "The other number is either the groups or the size of each group."

slides.title: Sharing or grouping?
slides.text: Read each story out loud. Decide. Then act one out with beans.

items.q: Stoick splits 54 arrows equally among 9 warriors. How many does each warrior get? Type sharing or grouping.
items.why: You know the groups (9 warriors). You find how many each gets.
items.no: Is 9 the number of warriors, or the arrows each one gets?

items.q: Hiccup ties 54 arrows into bundles of 9. How many bundles? Type sharing or grouping.
items.why: You know the size of each bundle (9). You find how many bundles.
items.no: Is 9 the number of bundles, or how many go in each bundle?

items.q: Toothless eats 7 fish a day. How many days will 63 fish last? Type sharing or grouping.
items.why: Each day is a group of 7 fish. You find how many days (groups).
items.no: 7 fish go in each day. What are you finding?

items.q: 63 fish are split evenly over 7 days. How many fish each day? Type sharing or grouping.
items.why: You know there are 7 days (groups). You find how many in each.
items.no: Do you know how many days there are?

notes.do: She acts out the Toothless story with beans: 63 beans, one pile of 7 per day. Then the last story with 7 plates. Same beans, two stories.
notes.ask: "What does your answer count: fish, or days?"
notes.listen: The Toothless one is the hardest: "a day" hides the group. If she says sharing, ask: "Do you know how many days? Or how many fish in each day?"

slides.title: Confirm it: check by multiplying
slides.text: A good mathematician does not trust an answer until it is confirmed. Multiply the quotient by the divisor. You should get back the dividend.

steps.text: 72 ÷ 8 = 9? 9 × 8 = 72 ✔ It matches, so it is right.
Snotlout wrote 54 ÷ 6 = 8. Check: 8 × 6 = 48. 48 is not 54 ✘. Try 9: 9 × 6 = 54 ✔. So 54 ÷ 6 = 9.
With a remainder: 43 ÷ 8 = 5 R 3. Check: 5 × 8 = 40, then 40 + 3 = 43 ✔

slides.tip: If the check does not give you the dividend, the answer is wrong. Fix it before you move on.

notes.do: Write the rule on the whiteboard: quotient × divisor (+ remainder) = dividend. Leave it up.
notes.ask: On the remainder step: "Where did the 3 go? Why do we add it back?" (Those beans were left in your hand; they are still part of the 43.)
notes.listen: She can say the rule back in her own words: "Multiply my answer by what I divided by, add the leftovers, and I should get the start number."

items.q: Hiccup says 56 ÷ 7 = 9. Check it by multiplying. What do you find?
Fishlegs wrote 44 ÷ 7 = 6 R 2. Check it: 6 × 7 + 2 = ____
items.why: 6 × 7 = 42 and 42 + 2 = 44. It matches the dividend, so he is right.

items.q: Only one of these is correct. Check each one. Which is it?
items.why: 9 × 7 = 63, so 63 ÷ 7 = 9 is confirmed.

notes.do: She writes each check on the whiteboard before she answers.
notes.say: "Out loud, every time: my answer times the divisor, plus the leftovers."
notes.listen: On the 44 ÷ 7 item, a common slip is forgetting to add the remainder and saying 42. Point to the rule on the board.

slides.title: The unknown can hide anywhere
slides.text: In a division fact, the unknown can be the dividend, the divisor or the quotient. Use the fact family to find it.

steps.text: ? ÷ 8 = 9. The dividend is missing. It is the biggest number: 9 × 8 = 72.
63 ÷ ? = 9. The divisor is missing. Ask: 9 × what = 63? 9 × 7 = 63, so the unknown is 7.

slides.tip: Ask first: which number is missing, the dividend, the divisor or the quotient?

notes.do: She covers the matching corner on one of her fact family cards for each step.
notes.ask: "Which part is missing: the dividend, the divisor or the quotient?" "If the dividend is missing, do we multiply or divide?" (multiply).
notes.listen: The trap is adding (8 + 9 = 17). If she adds, ask: "Which number in a family is always the biggest?"

items.q: ? ÷ 7 = 6. What is the unknown?
items.why: The dividend is quotient × divisor: 6 × 7 = 42. Confirm: 42 ÷ 7 = 6.

items.q: 56 ÷ ? = 8. What is the unknown?
A fact family has 7 and 56. The biggest number is 56. What is the third number?
items.why: 7 × 8 = 56, so the family is 7, 8 and 56.
no: 392 is 7 × 56. But 56 is the biggest number in this family.

notes.ask: For each: "Which part is missing?" before she answers.
notes.listen: She names the part and the operation: "dividend missing, so I multiply."

slides.title: Division detective steps
slides.text: Tap the steps in the order you use them for a division story.
steps: Interpret: is it sharing or grouping?
Write the division: total ÷ the number you know
Write the confirmed answer with a label (fish, nests, days)
slides.why: Read, interpret, divide, use a fact, confirm, then label the confirmed answer. That is the whole routine.
slides.hint: You cannot divide until you know what the story asks. What comes before writing the division?

notes.do: She says all six steps from memory before tapping. Write them as she says them on the whiteboard; they stay up for the story problems.
notes.ask: "Why does confirming come before writing the answer with a label?"
notes.listen: Read, interpret, divide, fact, confirm, label.

slides.title: Story problems
slides.text: Use the detective steps out loud on each one.

items.q: The Hooligans have 72 shields. They hang 8 on each ship. How many ships get shields?
items.why: Grouping: 72 ÷ 8 = 9 ships. Confirm: 9 × 8 = 72.
items.no: Interpret first: is 8 the ships, or the shields on each ship?

items.q: Hiccup trains 9 dragons. He has 81 treats to share equally. How many treats does each dragon get?
items.why: Sharing: 81 ÷ 9 = 9 treats each. Confirm: 9 × 9 = 81.

items.q: Fishlegs has 59 rocks. He puts 9 in each bag. How many bags can he fill, and how many rocks are left?
no: 9 × 7 = 63. That is more rocks than he has.
14 left is more than 9. Another bag can be filled.
50 is 59 − 9. That is subtracting, not dividing.

notes.do: She points to each detective step on the whiteboard as she uses it.
notes.ask: "Sharing or grouping?" "How do you confirm it?" "What is the label?"
notes.listen: A full answer sounds like: "Grouping. 72 ÷ 8 = 9. 9 × 8 = 72, confirmed. 9 ships."

items.q: Hiccup worked hard to decipher what the dragon was saying. What was he doing?
items.why: To decipher is to figure out something hard to understand.
no: Deciphering is about understanding, not volume.
Copying does not mean you understand it.
Ignoring is the opposite of working to understand.

items.q: Which sentence uses divisible correctly?
choices: 54 is divisible by 8, with 6 left over.
items.why: 9 × 6 = 54 with nothing left over, so 54 is divisible by 9.
no: Check: 7 × 8 = 56. 54 ÷ 7 = 7 R 5, so 54 is not divisible by 7.
If something is left over, it is not divisible.

items.q: Be ____: 45 ÷ 6 is 7 R 3, not just "about 7." Type the word from your word cards that means exactly right in every detail.
items.why: Precise means exactly right, with every detail correct.

notes.ask: "What clue in the sentence helped?" Then: "Use daunting in a sentence about the break."
notes.listen: For divisible, she uses Tuesday's idea: no remainder.

slides.title: Show me before you go
slides.text: On your own. No help this time.

items.q: 48 Vikings form 6 equal teams. How many on each team? Type sharing or grouping.
items.why: You know there are 6 teams (groups). You find how many on each.
items.no: Do you know how many teams there are?

items.q: ? ÷ 9 = 8. What is the unknown?

items.why: 7 × 7 = 49 and 49 + 1 = 50. It matches, so the answer is confirmed.

notes.listen: All three right means she is ready for the after-class lesson and the break work.
